statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 13% (low), Stress 43% (moderate), Confidence 84% (high). Shared assessment for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON. Conditional risk is concentrated in a narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC band spanning the U.S. cash open, the Richmond Fed survey and the Williams and Jefferson remarks; that band is published as the danger window instead of the whole session. A lighter second checkpoint sits at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and Barkin remarks, and a third in the 19:00 UTC power hour, which held the highest Tail reading of the past 24 hours. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping. The reading would change on observed persistent one-way structure: shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ holding near a session extreme, or aligned yields, VIX, oil, semiconductors and breadth confirming a single direction.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold mid-range and marginally below settlement with both overnight extremes rejected; a 14.63 VIX, four lower Treasury yield points and a deepening oil slide on Strait of Hormuz de-escalation keep tail risk low as the U.S. cash open passes unobserved in delayed feeds
body: Monday closed with the Nasdaq-100 cash index at a record 30,482.35, up 2.83% inside a 29,933.22-30,557.33 day range, as an AI and semiconductor rally lifted the Nasdaq Composite 2.26% to a record 27,122.09. Leadership was narrow but powerful: AMD rose about 10% to become the fourth U.S. chipmaker worth $1 trillion, Intel gained about 12%, Qualcomm more than 9% and Meta about 11% on the reception of its Muse AI app. Today the NQ Dec-26 contract has traded a 30,670.00-30,916.50 range against a 30,784.75 prior settlement and sits at 30,761.75-30,769.75, down 0.05-0.07%. Two independent quote sources agree on both the level and the settlement reference. Price holding the middle of that range after both extremes were rejected is direct evidence that retracement is functioning in both directions, and that is the main reason Tail stays low despite the size of Monday's advance. One limitation is stated plainly: the 13:30 UTC cash open falls inside the current clock hour, but the delayed CME feeds available here are timestamped 13:16-13:18 UTC, so the opening auction's structure is not yet observable. It is therefore carried as an unobserved checkpoint rather than scored as continuation, and Confidence is set at 84 rather than higher for that reason. Cross-asset evidence points the same way rather than amplifying. The VIX is 14.63, down 1.61% from a 14.87 close and confined to a 14.62-14.95 band. All four Treasury points are lower: the 2-year at 4.75%, the 5-year at 4.81%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the 30-year at 5.27%, with the 5-year off the most at about 2.1 basis points. Easing yields remove the tightening channel that normally accompanies a one-way equity trend. WTI is $89.95, down 2.62%, and Brent $98.29, down 2.04%, a fifth consecutive lower session. Two independent de-escalation vectors sit behind that move. Reporting today says a senior Iranian official has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure and lifts its blockade, delivered through mediators; separately, U.S. Central Command has said crude and LNG flows through the strait have reached a six-month high with the main transit lanes clear of mines. Washington has not publicly accepted Tehran's conditions, so this is treated as a live two-sided headline risk rather than a resolved one. A second policy vector emerged over the weekend: Treasury Secretary Bessent described roughly eight hours of talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng as very successful, with proposals for a U.S.-China AI dialogue and a trade board, ahead of a Trump-Xi summit on 24 September in Washington. That summit is a verified forward catalyst but no exact time could be confirmed, so it is deliberately omitted from the structured event list rather than published with a guessed timestamp, and is instead carried as a checkpoint in the hourly drivers. The scheduled load today is moderate and clustered: the Richmond Fed manufacturing survey at 14:00 UTC, Williams at 14:05 and Jefferson at 14:20, then the 2-year note auction and Barkin at 17:00. None is an automatic block, though the rate path is genuinely live and speaker headlines can move yields and the AI complex together. A note on source hygiene: the aggregated economic calendar consulted for this run displayed populated actual values for releases still days in the future, which is a parsing artefact of its previous-period column; no release outcome from that table has been treated as verified or published as news. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was likewise not used as evidence: its payload is about three hours old against a 90-minute freshness bar, its collection status is partial, and its futures and calendar sections are unavailable, so the assessment rests entirely on independently fetched primary sources. The dominant mode is normal. None of the Tail amplifiers is present: there is no persistent directional efficiency, no sequence of failed retracements, no repeated extension and no holding near a session extreme. Stress at 43 reflects the record-close starting point, narrow leadership, the clustered speaker block now beginning, and the unobserved cash open. Confidence at 84 reflects current verified levels for futures, volatility, four yield points and both oil benchmarks, a cross-checked event calendar and two verified geopolitical and policy stories, less the missing post-open price path.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours contain a complete set of 24 published hourly assessments. Tail built steadily through Monday's U.S. session as the index trended to a record close, peaking at 33 with Stress at 57 in the 19:00 UTC hour, which mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES from 14:00 through 19:00 UTC. After the cash close the trend-up characterisation gave way to a normal, two-way regime: Tail fell to 23 by 20:00 UTC and to 14 by 21:00 UTC, then held an 11-13 band through the entire Asian and European overnight, with Stress between 28 and 39 and Confidence between 85 and 87. Every hour from 21:00 UTC onward mapped to EA_ON, and the final six hours sat at Tail 12-13 with Stress 36-39. Nothing in that sequence has been revised with later information.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail inside a 10-17 band, so every forecast hour maps to EA_ON. Conditional risk is front-loaded into the 13:30-15:00 UTC band covering the cash open, the Richmond Fed survey and the Williams and Jefferson remarks, where Tail peaks at 17 and Stress at 48. Lighter secondary checkpoints follow at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction with Barkin, and in the 19:00 UTC power hour that carried Monday's highest Tail reading. From the 20:00 UTC cash close the path assumes liquidity drains and Tail decays to a 10-11 overnight floor, then rebuilds gradually to 14 at the end of the window as Wednesday's high-impact S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC and the following cash open come into view. Confidence decays from 84 to 69 across the window because live price-path evidence beyond the current hour is projected rather than observed.
